title: Mesh golden-signal pipeline and probabilistic admission runbook
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Build a cross-region ‘mesh’ ingestion and enrichment pipeline for golden signals (request-rate, errors, saturation, token-latency) that powers a probabilistic admission controller and an operator-focused runbook. This ticket scopes the instrumentation, dashboard surfaces, sampling strategy, and a staged rollout plan for activating probabilistic shedding and automated threshold tuning. Goal: give SREs and on-call engineers a single observable source-of-truth for token-level latency SLI calculation, admission decisions, and failover telemetry so we can safely enable regional probabilistic shedding without manual tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Mesh pipeline ingests per-token timing events from all regions and normalizes them into a canonical event with fields: request_id, shard, region, sequence_length_bucket, token_index, decode_ms, kv_hit, admission_score
Token-level SLI (p50/p95/p99) computed daily and streaming at 1min rollups for each region and per-priority path
Dashboards: Overview (global), Regional breakdown, Admission decision log, Failure-mode drilldown — links accessible to SREs and PMs
Probabilistic admission controller can be toggled in staging and uses live SLI deltas + synthetic prober to adjust admission probability within 5 minutes
Runbook documented with play steps, rollback criteria, and example queries; disaster test executed in chaos-week with no more than 2 customer-facing incidents
End-to-end latency telemetry pipeline tolerates 10% event loss without biasing SLI calculations (test harness in synthetic job)
implementation_notes: Instrumentation: extend existing token-timing hooks to emit compact events (protobuf) to the mesh collector; include a 128-bit trace/request id and a 16-bit sequence bucket

Sampling: deterministic reservoir per-tenant with head-sampling for cold-start traces and tail-sampling for sequences above 512 tokens; default sample rate 1/20 for standard traffic, adjustable per-customer
Enrichment: join event stream with admit-score and shard-load metadata in the collector so dashboards can attribute decisions to admission heuristics
Aggregators: compute streaming q-digests per (region, priority, sequence_bucket) to produce p50/p95/p99 without full event retention
Storage/retention: 90 days coarse-grained (1min rollups), 7 days of full event retention for incident replay
Admission autotuner: implement a hill-climb optimizer that uses recent SLI slope and synthetic-probe feedback to nudge probability +/- up to 20% per minute
Safety: admission controller must fall back to a safe-config (100% allow or previously known-good probability) on loss of mesh heartbeat or if synthetic probe p99 degrades > 2x
Backwards compat: provide an opt-in flag for Dedicated customers to surface enriched events to their private sinks only
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Dev: collector + small aggregator in staging, emit canonical events from toy runtime (2 weeks)
Phase 2 - Pilot: enable on 5% of ingress across two non-critical regions; run in observe-only mode for admission decisions (3 weeks)
Phase 3 - Canary: probabilistic admission active at low rate (max 10% shed) in staging and then 1 production region; monitor synthetic probes and SLI windows (2 weeks)
Phase 4 - Gradual: expand to multi-region with autotuner enabled, limit autotune delta to +/-20% per 10m; runbook sign-off required before global activation (3 weeks)
Phase 5 - Postmortem: run chaos tests and collect incident data; if any customer-impacting regression, revert and increase safety constraints
monitoring_queries: Prometheus (example): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_decode_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, priority))
Admission log query: count() by (admit_result, region, priority) over 10m and correlate with kv_prefetch_hit_rate
Synthetic probe alert: if synthetic-p99 / baseline-p99 > 1.5 for 3 consecutive minutes => trigger P1 runbook
Bias check: compare sampled vs unsampled p95 on control-slab; alert if divergence > 10%
